facts.fact: Paratus Group (press release republished by ITWeb Africa) says it switched on on 2026-02-09 the 2,000km protected terrestrial G2M fibre route from Goma in eastern DRC via Kigali (Rwanda), Kampala (Uganda) and Nairobi (Kenya) to Mombasa on the coast, now live and carrying traffic, linking DRC to coastal subsea cable capacity.

Paratus says the G2M Goma-Mombasa route is already carrying traffic for its first wholesale customers and is designed for carriers, ISPs and enterprises, i.e. operators other than the owner buy capacity on it.

facts.fact: Airtel Congo RDC SA says it became the first operator in DRC to put the first phase of the 2Africa submarine cable into service, activating an initial 200 Gbps on 2025-12-18; the document names no landing station.

Agence Ecofin, citing TeleGeography's Submarine Cable Map, says two systems land at Moanda, DRC's cable landing: 2Africa (commercial service in DRC with 200 Gbps activated by Airtel on 2025-12-18) and WACS (in service since 2012, serving DRC); both at the same landing point, so two routes, not independent.

facts.fact: Congo Telecom said the WACS submarine cable segment linking the DRC and the Republic of Congo was recommissioned on 16 November 2026 after repairs, with the Matombi and Muanda landing stations supporting the work.
